quotes: Whole-genome multiple sequence alignment and pangenome graph analysis must reconcile quadratic pairwise scaling, sharp compositional skew, and rampant multigene duplication across divergent lineages. Standard workflows split these tasks across disconnected aligners, graph cleaners, liftover tools, and format-specific libraries that rely on fixed substitution matrices calibrated near balanced nucleotide composition and force base-by-base alignments through unalignable regions. Here we present Horizon, an information-theoretic genome alignment and pangenome graph suite implemented in Rust (`10` binaries in `src/bin/`, including the `horizon` subcommand dispatcher) that unifies pairwise alignment (`horizon_wga`), seeded sequence-to-graph DAG/POA alignment (`horizon_wga --graph`), log-linear multi-species merging (`horizon_merge`), progressive guide-tree alignment (`horizon_guide`), streaming `GFA v1.0/v1.1` inspection and extraction (`horizon_gfa`), graph-aware coordinate liftover (`horizon_lift`), junction cleaning (`horizon_clean`), and e-graph walk resolution (`horizon_resolve`). Horizon's alignment core combines compact strand-symmetric spaced-seed indexing (`FlatSeedIndex` with 16-bit prefix bucketing), Rayon-parallel transition seeding, and six-frame biochemical amino-acid seeding with Beta-Bernoulli Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection over local weak/strong hydrogen-bond channels, driving a three-state Minimum Description Length forward-backward aligner calibrated by Conformal Risk Control. Regions whose posterior homology support falls below the calibrated bit-savings floor are isolated as explicit Horizon Bubbles instead of being forced into spurious base pairs, while tandem duplications and nested inversions are collapsed non-destructively via MDL-calibrated equality saturation (`MdlCostModel`). Across verified UCSC/Ensembl/B10K reference-MAF slices (`horizon_eval` on MAF-concatenated `(ref_id, tgt_id)` pairs), multi-species progressive builds, and `12 GB` HPRC v1.0 Minigraph-Cactus pangenome benchmarks (`8cd5db0` / `2896229`), `horizon_wga` achieves `95.6%` recall / `97.4%` precision on `100-way chrM` (`hg38` × `panTro4`), `91.4%` recall / `87.0%` precision on `cactus447way` primates (`Macaca_mulatta`), `71.1%` recall / `95.1%` precision on `B10K 363-way` avian (`Gallus_gallus` × `Taeniopygia_guttata`), and `59.8%` recall / `78.5%` precision on `cactus241way chr22 1MB` (`Canis_lupus_familiaris`, `31` contigs in `0.852 s`) while reducing `18%`-GC random-DNA false-positive pairs from `18,077` to `0` on the `seed=999` benchmark draw (`80–448` pairs on `4/5` other seeds; `288` / `149` pairs on `30%` / `45%`-GC single draws); `horizon_merge` nets `92` vertebrate `chrM` species in `21.78 s` (`26.6 MB` RSS), and `horizon_guide --progressive --hal` (`2896229`) builds a `5`-mammal progressive MAF (`1,109` blocks) and a single-contig star-tree HDF5 `v0` HAL stub (`4` bottom segments) in `0.859 s`. On the `12 GB` HPRC v1.0 graph, counter-only `horizon_gfa stats` streams all `81.4M` segments in `196.93 s` at `96.9 MB` peak RSS, outperforming `vg v1.60.0` (`vg stats`, which builds an in-memory handle graph) in runtime (`0.08 s` vs. `4.2984 s`) and peak RSS (`22.6 MB` vs. `77.0 MB`) on a real `10,000`-segment (`10.94 Mbp`, `96.09%` `'N'`) `chr22` subgraph; and `horizon_wga --resolve-dups` aligns `GRCh38.chr6` (`170.8 Mbp`) × `CHM13.chr6` (`110.7 Mbp` q-arm `61.4M–172.1M`) in `258.88–267.86 s` (`8cd5db0`; `304.53 s` at `2896229` with multi-chain partitioning, `282.2M` aligned pairs, `98.9%` `CHM13` coverage) with **99.54%** base-coverage recall, **97.96%** exact base-coordinate recall, `48.63%` conditioned exact pair precision (`38.22%` unconditional across all `282.2M` emitted pairs) against `1.63M` `1-to-1` HPRC graph segments alongside `minimap2 -x asm5` (`46.95 s`, `2,947.5 MB` RSS, `99.71%` exact recall, `99.75%` conditioned / `99.60%` unconditional exact precision). Horizon is available at `https://github.com/richard-burhans/horizon-aligner`.

Horizon addresses these coupled bottlenecks in a unified, pure-Rust suite of ten composable executables in `src/bin/` (`horizon_wga` including `--graph`, `horizon_merge`, `horizon_guide`, `horizon_gfa`, `horizon_lift`, `horizon_clean`, `horizon_resolve`, `horizon_eval`, `bench_chr1`, and the `horizon <subcommand>` dispatcher). The alignment, merging, and resolution tools (`horizon_wga`, `horizon_guide`, `horizon_resolve`, `horizon_merge`, and `horizon_clean`) draw on shared MDL, BOCPD, e-graph, and GFA primitives (`horizon_clean` uses an ad-hoc Bernoulli/BIC changepoint score rather than `src/mdl/dp.rs`), while `horizon_gfa` and `horizon_lift` use the shared streaming GFA (`src/gfa/mod.rs`) and UCSC coordinate (`src/coord.rs`) modules without BOCPD/MDL/e-graph scoring, and `horizon` dispatches subcommands. Rather than delegating across external tools such as `vg` (Garrison et al. 2018), `odgi` (Guarracino et al. 2022), and `BEDTools` (Quinlan & Hall 2010), Horizon provides native streaming `GFA v1.0/v1.1` inspection, liftover, cleaning, e-graph walk resolution, and `MAF`, `rGFA`, and `HAL`-compatible interoperability in a single crate.

**Figure 1. Horizon integrates multi-tier strand-symmetric seeding, online compositional changepoint detection, conformal abstention, e-graph resolution, and streaming GFA pangenome tools into a unified pure-Rust suite.** Stages 1–2 chain `FlatSeedIndex` (`12 B/entry`, 16-bit prefix buckets), Rayon-parallel `LASTZ12` transition seeds, and biochemical six-frame `AA5` seeds into colinear LCBs or seeded DAG/POA components (`horizon_wga --graph`) while isolating unanchored spans as macro Horizon Bubbles. Stages 3–4 run Beta-Bernoulli BOCPD over the weak/strong (*W*) channel to parameterize flat `BandGrid` / topological DAG Minimum Description Length forward-backward alignment gated by Conformal Risk Control (`λ̂ = 10.0` bits). Stages 5–8 collapse duplications via `MdlCostModel` e-graphs (`horizon_resolve`, `--resolve-dups`), merge pairwise blocks in O(*N* log *N*) sweep-line time (`horizon_merge`, `horizon_guide`), stream `12 GB+` `GFA` graphs (`horizon_gfa`, `horizon_lift`, `horizon_clean`), and provide `MAF`, `rGFA`, and pure-Rust `HAL` interoperability (`horizon <subcommand>`). Visual dictionary: blue denotes seeding, chaining, and DAG construction; orange denotes adaptive MDL alignment; vermilion denotes conformal abstention; green denotes e-graph resolution and merging; purple denotes streaming GFA pangenome tools and format interoperability.

Between chained anchors, Horizon evaluates homology using a three-state Minimum Description Length forward-backward Pair-HMM aligner adapted from Allison, Wallace, and Yee (1992) and Durbin et al. (1998), with normalized outgoing transition probabilities and DAG/POA extensions following Lee et al. (2002) and Gao et al. (2021). Instead of allocating pointer-heavy sparse dictionaries, the Rust kernel stores log-space forward (α) and backward (β) tables in a contiguous flat `BandLayout` (`Vec<f64>`, stride `2 * band_w + 1`, default `band_w = 180`). It evaluates `logplus` transitions and per-column match posteriors `P(M_ij | X, Y)` in cache-friendly linear passes, followed by X-drop flank extension (`mdl_xdrop_extend_with_params`, `max_ext = 1500`).

Each candidate interval is summarized by its total description-length savings `ΔL = L_null − L_joint` in bits relative to independent BOCPD-parameterized null encoding, scaled by a Rissanen/BIC search-space complexity floor `0.55 * log2(N * M)` (Rissanen 1978; Schwarz 1978; Grünwald 2007). Using fixed Conformal Risk Control defaults calibrated offline at risk level `α = 0.07` (`n_cal = 15`; Angelopoulos et al. 2024), Horizon enforces a constant bit-savings floor `λ̂ = 10.0` bits (`min_delta_bits = 10.0`) and a minimum column posterior floor (`0.15`). Any interval or internal gap failing these floors is withheld from base-by-base alignment and emitted explicitly as a **Horizon Bubble** (`# HB:Z:` metadata in `GFA` and summary outputs); in graph cleaning (`horizon_clean`), `HB:i:1` marks severed discordant `L`-edges rather than full topological superbubble/ultrabubble or SPQR-tree decompositions (Paten et al. 2018; Sena et al. 2026).

2. `horizon_lift` (`src/bin/horizon_lift/main.rs`) lifts `BED` and `GFF3` intervals across haplotypes via two-pass `P`/`W` streaming, `--bridge-bp` micro-bubble coalescing, and `coord::Interval` UCSC reverse-strand arithmetic (`src/coord.rs`).

For multi-species panels, `horizon_merge` (`src/bin/horizon_merge.rs`) executes an O(*N* log *N*) coordinate sweep over pairwise `MAF` files against a selected reference or central hinge, applying best-score interval netting (`interval_match_score`; cf. Kent et al. 2003) and threading query insertion columns across all taxa into `MAF` and reference `rGFA` (`SN:Z`, `SO:i`, `SR:i:0`) graphs. For progressive guide-tree builds, `horizon_guide` (`src/bin/horizon_guide/main.rs`) performs identity-gated transitive sister-clade rescue (`rescue_transitive_maf`) and ancestral consensus bridging. Finally, `src/hal/` implements an in-memory hierarchical `HalAlignment` model (`TopSegment`, `BottomSegment`, reference-free `to_maf_for_genome`) alongside pure-Rust streaming `Read + Seek` HDF5 v0/v1 container inspection (`hdf5_read.rs`), B-tree group traversal, zlib chunk decompression (`flate2`), binary record decoders (`DNA_ARRAY`, `SEQIDX_ARRAY`, `SEQNAME_ARRAY`, `TOP_ARRAY`, `BOTTOM_ARRAY`), and a `libhdf5`-compatible HDF5 `v0` writer (`hdf5_write.rs`) with multi-level B-tree support (Hickey et al. 2013).

With zero parameter retuning, we evaluated `horizon_wga` across eight verified external reference-MAF slices spanning close primates, medium-divergence mammals, distant mammals, deep avian divergence (`B10K 363-way`), and mitochondrial genomes (`docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md`; Table 1). Following addition of the composition-aware BOCPD LCB gate (`joint_pair_bits - GAP_OPEN_BITS` across all LCB lengths in `src/mdl/mod.rs`), false-positive alignments on the `seed=999` `10,000`-bp random `18%`-GC draw dropped from `18,077` pairs (`74.9%` coverage) to `0` pairs (`0.0069 s`), whereas `4/5` other random `18%`-GC seeds still emitted `80–448` false-positive pairs and `30%`-GC and `45%`-GC single draws emitted `288` pairs (`0.4150 s`) and `149` pairs (`0.3829 s`). Note that `horizon_eval` evaluates MAF-concatenated `(ref_id, tgt_id)` contig pairs individually against reference `MAF` blocks (`LASTZ`, `Cactus`, `MULTIZ`, and `EPO`), nuclear slices were re-evaluated after LCB gate calibration, and head-to-head external pairwise aligner re-runs (`FastGA`, `LASTZ`, `KegAlign`) remain pending on the benchmark host (`minimap2 -x asm5` is compared on full `chr6` below). On tuning mitochondrial slices (`multiz100way chrM`), `horizon_wga` achieved `95.6%` recall and `97.4%` precision on human (`hg38`) × chimp (`panTro4`, `0.058 s`) and `76.5%` recall and `93.7%` precision on human × mouse (`mm10`, `0.064 s`). On held-out nuclear slices, `horizon_wga` achieved `91.4%` recall / `87.0%` precision on `cactus447way` macaque (`Macaca_mulatta`, `0.102 s`), `86.3%` recall / `87.7%` precision on `multiz470way` marmoset (`HLcalPym1`, `0.189 s`), `54.0%` recall / `67.6%` precision on `cactus447way` horse (`Equus_caballus`, `0.068 s`), `48.0%` recall / `83.3%` precision on `cactus241way` dog (`chr22_random`, `0.050 s`), `59.8%` recall / `78.5%` precision (`67.9%` F1) across `31` dog target contigs on `cactus241way chr22 1MB` (`0.852 s`, `2,076` Horizon Bubbles), and `71.1%` recall / `95.1%` precision on the `B10K 363-way` avian `chr1:5.9M–6.4M` slice (`Gallus_gallus` × `Taeniopygia_guttata`, `0.642 s`, `3,814` Horizon Bubbles).

On whole-chromosome `horizon_wga --resolve-dups` runs (`8cd5db0` / `2896229`; `n = 1` per run; `docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md`), `GRCh38.chr22` × `CHM13.chr22:15729460-51324926` finished in `69.10 s` (`3,971.6 MB` RSS, `34,165,619` aligned pairs, `unique_x_bp = 34,039,553`, `unique_y_bp = 34,020,579`, `95.6%` of `CHM13.chr22` q-arm, `21,787` Horizon Bubbles). On `GRCh38.chr6:65M–85M` × `CHM13.chr6:61M–81M` (`20 Mbp` q-arm), `FlatSeedIndex` + `BTreeSet`-indexed LCB clustering finished in `12.84 s` (`15,019,451` pairs, `16,417` bubbles). On full `GRCh38.chr6` (`170.8 Mbp`) × `CHM13.chr6` (`110.7 Mbp` q-arm `61401689–172126628`), `horizon_wga --resolve-dups` on `8cd5db0` completed in `258.88–267.86 s` (`2.21×` faster than `592.68 s` at `bb43dd9` and `3.97×` faster than `1,062.45 s` at `1e47fe0`; Figure 5) with `282,193,564` aligned pairs covering `124,160,423` bp (`72.7%`) of `GRCh38.chr6` and `109,464,447` bp (`98.9%`) of the `CHM13.chr6` q-arm (`178,737` Horizon Bubbles). With the multi-chain `partition_colinear_blocks` fix (`2896229`, `304.53 s`), comparing Horizon's many-to-many `chr6` MAF (`370,937` blocks, `282,163,046` pairs) base-for-base against the `1,628,018` `1-to-1` shared segments (`110,082,990` bp) between `GRCh38.chr6` and `CHM13.chr6:61401689–172126628` in the HPRC Minigraph-Cactus graph yields **99.54%** base-coverage recall, **97.96%** exact coordinate recall (`107,836,669 / 110,082,990` bp; `98.14%` within `1 kb`), `48.63%` conditioned exact pair precision on `pairs_on_hprc_1to1_x` (`107,836,669 / 221,734,653`; `~2.01×` local multiplicity), and **38.22%** unconditional exact pair precision across all `282,163,046` emitted pairs (`60,428,393` / `21.42%` outside `1-to-1` HPRC segments; `~2.58×` overall multiplicity), compared to `minimap2 -x asm5` (`v2.28-r1209`, `46.95 s`, `2,947.5 MB` RSS, `1-to-1` primary alignments: `99.71%` exact recall, `99.75%` conditioned / `99.60%` unconditional exact precision; Figure 7).

On a real sequence-bearing `10,000`-segment HPRC `chr22` subgraph (`10,937,960` bp total, of which `10,510,000` bp / `96.09%` are `'N'` bases in segment `76067108` and `427,960` bp are ACGT across `chr22`, `chrUn_GL000224v1`, and `chr14_KI270722v1_random`; `10,300` links, `1` path, `4` walks; Figure 6A), counter-only `horizon_gfa stats` ran in `0.08 s` at `22.6 MB` peak RSS, compared with `vg stats -z -l -N` (`vg v1.60.0`: `4.2984 s`, `77.0 MB` RSS) and `vg convert -g -p` (`1.8292 s`, `76.6 MB` RSS), which construct full in-memory handle graphs (`odgi` and `gfatools` baselines remain pending). On the same HPRC subgraph, `horizon_clean --min-cp-bits 10.0` ran in `0.13 s` (`33.4 MB` RSS, keeping all `10,300` valid walk links), `horizon_resolve --collapse-dups --tag-walks` processed `223` anchors and `755` snarl/bubble windows in `5.571 s` (`23.6 MB` RSS, emitting `W`-line `EG:Z:` tags rather than `# EG:Z:` comments), and `horizon_wga --graph` (`20,000` bidirected DAG nodes) ran in `2.98–6.09 s` (`153.9–154.6 MB` RSS), abstaining (`aligned_pairs = 0`) on a `400`-bp all-`N` query and aligning `122/258` bp (`6` bubbles) and `197/356` bp (`8` bubbles) on real HPRC walk queries. For multi-species panels (`n = 1` runs without reference-MAF accuracy verification), `horizon_merge` netted `92` vertebrate `chrM` (`~16.5 kb`) species in `21.78 s` (`26.6 MB` RSS, `460` multi-species blocks), and `horizon_guide --progressive --hal --rbest` (`2896229`) aligned `5` mammals (`hg38`, `Macaca_mulatta`, `HLcalPym1`, `Equus_caballus`, `Canis_lupus`) in `0.859 s` (`1,109` MAF blocks, `967` multi-species, plus a single-contig star-tree HDF5 `v0` HAL stub of `4` bottom segments inspected via `horizon_wga --hal-info`). All `97` active Rust unit tests (plus `1` ignored `.hal` integration test; `98` total) pass on `HEAD` with zero `clippy` warnings.

**Figure 6. Head-to-head HPRC `10k`-segment subgraph comparison against `vg v1.60.0`, multi-species suite scaling, and BOCPD LCB gate calibration.** **A.** Log-log wall-clock runtime versus peak RSS across the `10,000`-segment (`10.94 Mbp`, `96.09%` `'N'`) real HPRC `chr22` subgraph (`horizon_gfa stats` counter-only vs. `vg stats` / `vg convert` in-memory graph construction, plus `horizon_clean`, `horizon_wga --graph`, and `horizon_resolve`) and multi-species `horizon_merge` (`92`-species `chrM`) and `horizon_guide` (`5`-species `--progressive --hal`). **B.** Effect of the `R1-HMM` composition-aware BOCPD LCB gate (`joint_pair_bits - GAP_OPEN_BITS`): on the `seed=999` `18%`-GC `10`-kb null draw, pairs drop from `18,077` to `0` (`80–448` pairs remain on `4/5` other seeds) while nuclear precision shifts across horse (`65.4%` → `67.6%`), macaque (`84.6%` → `87.0%`), and marmoset (`86.1%` → `87.7%`). Visual dictionary: in Panel A, purple denotes `horizon_gfa`, green denotes `horizon_clean`/`horizon_merge`, blue/sky blue denote `horizon_wga --graph`/`horizon_guide`, orange denotes `horizon_resolve`, and vermilion/gray denote `vg`; in Panel B, gray denotes pre-gate and blue denotes post-gate.

**Figure 7. Horizon's `GRCh38.chr6` × `CHM13.chr6` q-arm alignment achieves `97.96%` exact base-coordinate recall against the HPRC Minigraph-Cactus graph alongside `minimap2 -x asm5`.** **A.** Whole-chromosome synteny dot-plot (`GRCh38.chr6` `0–170.8 Mbp` vs. `CHM13.chr6` q-arm `61.4–172.1 Mbp`) overlaying HPRC `1-to-1` shared segments (`≥500` bp, sky blue) and Horizon MAF blocks (`≥2` kb, dark blue); the dashed orange line marks the `61 Mbp` q-arm boundary. **B.** Agreement with `1,628,018` HPRC `1-to-1` shared segments (`110,082,990` bp) for many-to-many `horizon_wga` (`99.5%` base-coverage recall, `98.0%` exact `0`-bp recall, `98.1%` `≤1`-kb recall, `48.6%` conditioned exact pair precision [`38.2%` unconditional across `282.2M` pairs]) vs. `1-to-1` primary `minimap2 -x asm5` (`100.0%` base-coverage recall, `99.7%` exact recall, `99.8%` conditioned [`99.6%` unconditional] exact precision). **C.** `1 Mbp`-binned exact (`Δy = 0` bp) recall along `GRCh38.chr6` (`n = 171` bins) comparing HPRC `1-to-1` shared bp (gray fill), `minimap2 -x asm5` (dashed orange), and Horizon (solid blue) across the `58–62 Mbp` centromeric boundary (shaded orange) and the entire `q`-arm.

Three concrete steps define our immediate roadmap. First, while de novo precision remains high (`87–97%`) across close and medium divergences, recall drops to `54–62%` on distant mammalian slices (`cactus447way` horse and `cactus241way` dog), motivating iterative ancestral consensus scaling in `horizon_guide` across deeper vertebrate clades. quotes: Whole-genome multiple sequence alignment and pangenome graph analysis must reconcile quadratic pairwise scaling, sharp compositional skew, and rampant multigene duplication across divergent lineages. Standard workflows split these tasks across disconnected aligners, graph cleaners, liftover tools, and format-specific libraries that rely on fixed substitution matrices calibrated near balanced nucleotide composition and force base-by-base alignments through unalignable regions. Here we present Horizon, an information-theoretic genome alignment and pangenome graph suite implemented in Rust (`10` binaries in `src/bin/`, including the `horizon` subcommand dispatcher) that unifies pairwise alignment (`horizon_wga`), seeded sequence-to-graph DAG/POA alignment (`horizon_wga --graph`), log-linear multi-species merging (`horizon_merge`), progressive guide-tree alignment (`horizon_guide`), streaming `GFA v1.0/v1.1` inspection and extraction (`horizon_gfa`), graph-aware coordinate liftover (`horizon_lift`), junction cleaning (`horizon_clean`), and e-graph walk resolution (`horizon_resolve`). Horizon's alignment core combines compact strand-symmetric spaced-seed indexing (`FlatSeedIndex` with 16-bit prefix bucketing), Rayon-parallel transition seeding, and six-frame biochemical amino-acid seeding with Beta-Bernoulli Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection over local weak/strong hydrogen-bond channels, driving a three-state Minimum Description Length forward-backward aligner calibrated by Conformal Risk Control. Regions whose posterior homology support falls below the calibrated bit-savings floor are isolated as explicit Horizon Bubbles instead of being forced into spurious base pairs, while tandem duplications and nested inversions are collapsed non-destructively via MDL-calibrated equality saturation (`MdlCostModel`). Across verified UCSC/Ensembl/B10K reference-MAF slices (`horizon_eval` on MAF-concatenated `(ref_id, tgt_id)` pairs), multi-species progressive builds, and `12 GB` HPRC v1.0 Minigraph-Cactus pangenome benchmarks (`8cd5db0` / `2896229`), `horizon_wga` achieves `95.6%` recall / `97.4%` precision on `100-way chrM` (`hg38` × `panTro4`), `91.4%` recall / `87.0%` precision on `cactus447way` primates (`Macaca_mulatta`), `71.1%` recall / `95.1%` precision on `B10K 363-way` avian (`Gallus_gallus` × `Taeniopygia_guttata`), and `59.8%` recall / `78.5%` precision on `cactus241way chr22 1MB` (`Canis_lupus_familiaris`, `31` contigs in `0.852 s`) while reducing `18%`-GC random-DNA false-positive pairs from `18,077` to `0` on the `seed=999` benchmark draw (`80–448` pairs on `4/5` other seeds; `288` / `149` pairs on `30%` / `45%`-GC single draws); `horizon_merge` nets `92` vertebrate `chrM` species in `21.78 s` (`26.6 MB` RSS), and `horizon_guide --progressive --hal` (`2896229`) builds a `5`-mammal progressive MAF (`1,109` blocks) and a single-contig star-tree HDF5 `v0` HAL stub (`4` bottom segments) in `0.859 s`. On the `12 GB` HPRC v1.0 graph, counter-only `horizon_gfa stats` streams all `81.4M` segments in `196.93 s` at `96.9 MB` peak RSS, outperforming `vg v1.60.0` (`vg stats`, which builds an in-memory handle graph) in runtime (`0.08 s` vs. `4.2984 s`) and peak RSS (`22.6 MB` vs. `77.0 MB`) on a real `10,000`-segment (`10.94 Mbp`, `96.09%` `'N'`) `chr22` subgraph; and `horizon_wga --resolve-dups` aligns `GRCh38.chr6` (`170.8 Mbp`) × `CHM13.chr6` (`110.7 Mbp` q-arm `61.4M–172.1M`) in `258.88–267.86 s` (`8cd5db0`; `304.53 s` at `2896229` with multi-chain partitioning, `282.2M` aligned pairs, `98.9%` `CHM13` coverage) with **99.54%** base-coverage recall, **97.96%** exact base-coordinate recall, `48.63%` conditioned exact pair precision (`38.22%` unconditional across all `282.2M` emitted pairs) against `1.63M` `1-to-1` HPRC graph segments alongside `minimap2 -x asm5` (`46.95 s`, `2,947.5 MB` RSS, `99.71%` exact recall, `99.75%` conditioned / `99.60%` unconditional exact precision). Horizon is available at `https://github.com/richard-burhans/horizon-aligner`.

Horizon addresses these coupled bottlenecks in a unified, pure-Rust suite of ten composable executables in `src/bin/` (`horizon_wga` including `--graph`, `horizon_merge`, `horizon_guide`, `horizon_gfa`, `horizon_lift`, `horizon_clean`, `horizon_resolve`, `horizon_eval`, `bench_chr1`, and the `horizon <subcommand>` dispatcher). The alignment, merging, and resolution tools (`horizon_wga`, `horizon_guide`, `horizon_resolve`, `horizon_merge`, and `horizon_clean`) draw on shared MDL, BOCPD, e-graph, and GFA primitives (`horizon_clean` uses an ad-hoc Bernoulli/BIC changepoint score rather than `src/mdl/dp.rs`), while `horizon_gfa` and `horizon_lift` use the shared streaming GFA (`src/gfa/mod.rs`) and UCSC coordinate (`src/coord.rs`) modules without BOCPD/MDL/e-graph scoring, and `horizon` dispatches subcommands. Rather than delegating across external tools such as `vg` (Garrison et al. 2018), `odgi` (Guarracino et al. 2022), and `BEDTools` (Quinlan & Hall 2010), Horizon provides native streaming `GFA v1.0/v1.1` inspection, liftover, cleaning, e-graph walk resolution, and `MAF`, `rGFA`, and `HAL`-compatible interoperability in a single crate.

**Figure 1. Horizon integrates multi-tier strand-symmetric seeding, online compositional changepoint detection, conformal abstention, e-graph resolution, and streaming GFA pangenome tools into a unified pure-Rust suite.** Stages 1–2 chain `FlatSeedIndex` (`12 B/entry`, 16-bit prefix buckets), Rayon-parallel `LASTZ12` transition seeds, and biochemical six-frame `AA5` seeds into colinear LCBs or seeded DAG/POA components (`horizon_wga --graph`) while isolating unanchored spans as macro Horizon Bubbles. Stages 3–4 run Beta-Bernoulli BOCPD over the weak/strong (*W*) channel to parameterize flat `BandLayout` / topological DAG Minimum Description Length forward-backward alignment gated by Conformal Risk Control (`λ̂ = 10.0` bits). Stages 5–8 collapse duplications via `MdlCostModel` e-graphs (`horizon_resolve`, `--resolve-dups`), merge pairwise blocks in O(*N* log *N*) sweep-line time (`horizon_merge`, `horizon_guide`), stream `12 GB+` `GFA` graphs (`horizon_gfa`, `horizon_lift`, `horizon_clean`), and provide `MAF`, `rGFA`, and pure-Rust `HAL` interoperability (`horizon <subcommand>`). Visual dictionary: blue denotes seeding, chaining, and DAG construction; orange denotes adaptive MDL alignment; vermilion denotes conformal abstention; green denotes e-graph resolution and merging; purple denotes streaming GFA pangenome tools and format interoperability.

Divergent genomes lose exact nucleotide *k*-mer identity rapidly, especially across synonymous coding positions and transitions. Modern fast aligners and *k*-mer counters such as `minimap2` (Li 2018), `KMC 3` (Kokot et al. 2017), `FastGA` (Myers et al. 2025), and `KegAlign` (Gulhan et al. 2025) accelerate indexing through minimizer, super-*k*-mer, or diagonal-partitioned schemes. Horizon pairs compact strand-symmetric spaced-seed indexing (`FlatSeedIndex` in `src/seeding/flat_index.rs`, `12 bytes/entry` post-build with 16-bit prefix bucketing and SDUST repeat masking via Morgulis et al. 2006) with transition-tolerant nucleotide and biochemical amino-acid seeds (`src/seeding/`). First, canonical `fwd.min(rc)` 2-bit `u64` spaced-seed indexing yields orientation-invariant keys across spaced masks (`MASK_PRIMARY_11_15` `111011011011011` at weight `11`, `MASK_PH11_18` `111010010100110111` from Ma et al. 2002, and `MASK_W10` `11011011011011` at weight `10`). Second, high-scoring pair gating and Rayon-parallel chunked scanning activate `LASTZ`-style `11`-mer and `12`-mer single- and double-transition seeds (`MASK_LASTZ11`, `MASK_LASTZ12` at *T* ∈ {1, 2}), purine-pyrimidine `RY20` seeds, and weak/strong `W10` seeds.

Between chained anchors, Horizon evaluates homology using a three-state Minimum Description Length forward-backward Pair-HMM aligner adapted from Allison, Wallace, and Yee (1992) and Durbin et al. (1998), with normalized outgoing transition probabilities and DAG/POA extensions following Lee et al. (2002) and Gao et al. (2021). Instead of allocating pointer-heavy sparse dictionaries, the Rust kernel stores log-space forward (α) and backward (β) tables in a contiguous flat `BandLayout` (`Vec<f64>`, stride `2 * band_w + 1`, default `band_w = 180`). It evaluates `logplus` transitions and per-column match posteriors `P(M_ij | X, Y)` in cache-friendly linear passes, followed by X-drop flank extension (`mdl_xdrop_extend_with_params`, `max_ext = 1500`).

Each candidate interval is summarized by its total description-length savings `ΔL = L_null − L_joint` in bits relative to independent BOCPD-parameterized null encoding, scaled by a Rissanen/BIC search-space complexity floor `0.55 * log2(N * M)` (Rissanen 1978; Schwarz 1978; Grünwald 2007). Using fixed Conformal Risk Control defaults calibrated offline at risk level `α = 0.07` (`n_cal = 15`; Angelopoulos et al. 2024), Horizon enforces a constant bit-savings floor `λ̂ = 10.0` bits (`min_delta_bits = 10.0`) and a minimum column posterior floor (`0.15`). Any interval or internal gap failing these floors is withheld from base-by-base alignment and emitted explicitly as a **Horizon Bubble** (`# HB:Z:` metadata in `GFA` and summary outputs); in graph cleaning (`horizon_clean`), `HB:i:1` marks severed discordant `L`-edges rather than full topological superbubble/ultrabubble or SPQR-tree decompositions (Paten et al. 2018; Sena et al. 2026).

2. `horizon_lift` (`src/bin/horizon_lift/main.rs`) lifts `BED` and `GFF3` intervals across haplotypes via two-pass `P`/`W` streaming, `--bridge-bp` micro-bubble coalescing, and `coord::Interval` UCSC reverse-strand arithmetic (`src/coord.rs`).

For multi-species panels, `horizon_merge` (`src/bin/horizon_merge.rs`) executes an O(*N* log *N*) coordinate sweep over pairwise `MAF` files against a selected reference or central hinge, applying best-score interval netting (`interval_match_score`; cf. Kent et al. 2003) and threading query insertion columns across all taxa into `MAF` and reference `rGFA` (`SN:Z`, `SO:i`, `SR:i:0`) graphs. For progressive guide-tree builds, `horizon_guide` (`src/bin/horizon_guide/main.rs`) performs identity-gated transitive sister-clade rescue (`rescue_transitive_maf`) and ancestral consensus bridging. Finally, `src/hal/` implements an in-memory hierarchical `HalAlignment` model (`TopSegment`, `BottomSegment`, reference-free `to_maf_for_genome`) alongside pure-Rust streaming `Read + Seek` HDF5 v0/v1 container inspection (`hdf5_read.rs`), B-tree group traversal, zlib chunk decompression (`flate2`), binary record decoders (`DNA_ARRAY`, `SEQIDX_ARRAY`, `SEQNAME_ARRAY`, `TOP_ARRAY`, `BOTTOM_ARRAY`), and a `libhdf5`-compatible HDF5 `v0` writer (`hdf5_write.rs`) with multi-level B-tree support (Hickey et al. 2013).
